A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same readable 13-page HumanOmni-Speaker paper, including all figures, tables, equations, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. Pages 2–13 render identically; page 1 differs only in authorship and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanOmni-Speaker evaluations in Tables 2–4 and ablation results in Table 5 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, speech-recognition, and ablation results in Tables 2–5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same architecture, 25-fps Visual Delta Encoder producing six tokens per frame, and three-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including the HumanOmni-Speaker benchmark tasks, LRS2/LRS3 speech recognition, and LibriSpeech evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 2–5, including Gemini3-Pro, Qwen3-Omni-flash, Qwen2.5-Omni-SFT, specialist speech models, and the Whisper-diarization plus Qwen3-VL pipeline.

E3.justification: The versions specify identical sample counts, Easy/Hard partitions, metrics, preprocessing, model configurations, and experimental procedures in Sections 3 and 5–7.

E4.justification: Both retain the same Grad-CAM analysis in Figure 4, encoder ablations and pipeline comparison in Table 5, and token-count and frame-rate sensitivity analyses in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports 0.8% speaker-localization error and 47.1%/28.5% VR-SDR SA-WER/IER for HumanOmni-Speaker in both versions.

T1.justification: The VR-SDR task definition and identity-fixed SA-WER and IER definitions, including Equations 1–2, are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the benchmark, Visual Delta Encoder, cross-modal alignment, and end-to-end lip-reading without cropping.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual shortcuts, motion capture, cross-modal binding, and preserved ASR capabilities are unchanged. No new limitations or applicability qualifications appear.

D1.justification: Architecture, annotation, and training details are unchanged. Both retain the same promise to release the benchmark, code, and checkpoints upon acceptance; no access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 41 references, and the positioning relative to prior speaker benchmarks and Omni models are identical.

P1.justification: The author list adds Jingren Zhou and places Zhiheng Ma before Xihan Wei. The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 23 March 2026 to v2 dated 29 April 2026. Body prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–5 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. Page layout is preserved; the first-page differences are author and version-stamp text edits.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only authorship and the arXiv stamp. Scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and document organization remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
